prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Story: KOSPI -8% Circuit Breaker Triggered: Cause, Duration, and U.S. ADR Read-Through. Related tickers: MU, TSM.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: South Korea's KOSPI fell almost 8% and the Korea Exchange suspended program trading — the most dramatic single-country move in the brief — but no cause (TSMC read-through? Samsung-specific? Macro?) or duration of the halt is specified, and U.S.-listed Korean ADRs are unaddressed.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What triggered South Korea's KOSPI to fall nearly 8% on October 15 2026 and the Korea Exchange to suspend program trading — was it primarily the TSMC earnings read-through, Samsung-specific news, or a macro/rate shock?
- How long did the Korea Exchange program-trading suspension last on October 15 2026, and what circuit-breaker threshold was breached?
- Did SK Hynix or Samsung Electronics issue any company-specific statements on October 15 2026 explaining their double-digit declines beyond the TSMC read-through?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## KOSPI / KRX [Cause and trading controls]

- The KOSPI opened at 5,673.01, down 5.59%, and closed at 5,554.22, down 454.59 points, or 7.57%, after reaching an intraday low of 5,450.81 on Oct. 15, 2026. (Yonhap, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[3]
- The reported drivers were a U.S. inflation shock, expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes, skepticism about the sustainability of AI-related investment, and selling in semiconductor stocks; the available reports did not identify Samsung-specific news as the primary trigger. (Chosun, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[1]
- U.S. September CPI rose 0.6% month over month and 3.7% year over year, versus a 3.6% economist estimate, according to the cited market report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[5]
- Foreign investors sold a net 284.7 billion won shortly after the Oct. 15 open, and the KOSPI recorded its seventh consecutive decline. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[5]
- The Korea Exchange activated a sell-side sidecar at 9:08 a.m. local time, equivalent to 8:08 p.m. ET on Oct. 14, suspending program trading for five minutes after KOSPI 200 futures fell at least 5% for one minute. (Korea JoongAng Daily, Oct. 15 09:41 a.m. local time; 20:41 ET Oct. 14)[6]
- The KOSPI Level 1 circuit breaker was activated at 12:38 p.m. local time, equivalent to 11:38 p.m. ET on Oct. 14, after the index fell 8.00% to 5,528.05 from the prior close of 6,008.81. (Korea JoongAng Daily, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[2]
- The circuit breaker halted KOSPI-listed-share trading for 20 minutes; after reopening, orders were matched through a 10-minute single-price auction. (Yonhap, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[7]
- The Level 1 circuit breaker threshold was an index decline of at least 8% from the previous session’s close that persisted for one minute; order entry was halted except for cancellations during the suspension. (Korea JoongAng Daily, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[2]
- The KOSDAQ circuit breaker was activated at approximately 12:23 p.m. local time, or 11:23 p.m. ET on Oct. 14, at 757.88, down 8.01%; the KOSPI breaker followed about 15 minutes later. (Korea JoongAng Daily, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[2]

## Samsung Electronics / SK Hynix [Company-specific disclosures]

- Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix were identified in the available reports as major semiconductor stocks contributing to the selloff, but the searched reports did not provide a company-specific statement from either company explaining the Oct. 15 declines beyond the AI, inflation, rate, and semiconductor-sector factors. (Yonhap, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[3]
- The available reports did not provide Oct. 15 analyst rating changes, price-target changes, or named analyst estimates for Samsung Electronics or SK Hynix. (Yonhap, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[3]

## TSM [Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing]

- Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was cited as the key global semiconductor reference point, with TSMC earnings described as a possible determinant of subsequent volatility; the available report did not establish TSMC earnings as the cause of the KOSPI circuit breaker. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[5]
- Mirae Asset Securities managing director Seo Sang-young said TSMC earnings were due later on Oct. 15 and would be the “turning point” for further volatility. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[5]
- TSM shares were reported down more than 2% premarket on Oct. 15 despite the company’s chief executive projecting no ceiling on profit growth; the report did not provide an exact price or time for the latest premarket reading. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[5]

## MU [Micron Technology]

- The available reports did not provide a specific Oct. 15–16, 2026 move, analyst action, earnings figure, guidance change, or company statement for Micron Technology. (Search results published Oct. 15, 2026; source publication times not stated)

## U.S.-listed Korean exposure [EWY]

- The iShares MSCI South Korea ETF was reported down approximately 7% across its U.S. close and after-hours session in connection with the Korean market selloff. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15; source publication time not stated)[5]
